title: Instance-adaptive TS augmentation (design-skill plan)
method: A parametric augmentation network learns per-instance views: a factorization mask h (hard-concrete relaxed Bernoulli per time step from a factorization head), a non-zero transformation mask g (transformation head) and noise η (random time-step masking of the encoder's first hidden layer); both heads share an input layer and a dilated-CNN extractor. The augmenter is trained with a Principle-of-Relevant-Information objective (β·expected L0 of h + mean-embedding discrepancy through the encoder) plus a temporal-consistency loss L_t (λ); the encoder is trained with L_global (InfoNCE) + α·L_local (subsequence contrast). Both are trained from scratch, alternating GAN-style (encoder every step, augmenter every M rounds), each with its own Adam optimizer.

claims.text: A factorization-based, information-theoretic definition of good views that preserves task-relevant information regardless of the downstream task while adding variance, with no prior domain knowledge
Learned per-instance views beat hand-picked views when the encoder and protocol are held fixed
The approach is encoder-agnostic and improves several contrastive learning backbones
The learned representations beat existing time-series representation learning methods on univariate and multivariate forecasting and on classification

questions.text: With a fixed contrastive backbone (TS2Vec) and evaluation protocol, does replacing hand-picked augmentations with the learned factorization-and-transformation augmentation improve downstream representation quality?
questions.hypothesis: On univariate forecasting (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, Electricity; frozen encoder, ridge probe), TS2Vec + learned augmentation gets lower test MSE averaged over horizons {24, 48, 168, 336, 720} than both TS2Vec with default augmentations and TS2Vec with the best hand-picked augmentation chosen on val; the paired per-seed difference has a 95% CI excluding 0 on at least 3 of the 4 datasets
questions.predictionIfFalse: The CIs include 0 or favor the baseline on 2 or more datasets

questions.text: Does the gain come from the learned masks, rather than from adding more stochastic augmentation?
questions.hypothesis: The learned masks beat random masks with matched sparsity and scale statistics (same expected ‖h‖₀ and distribution of g, no dependence on the instance)
questions.predictionIfFalse: H1 holds but H2 does not: the gain is just 'more augmentation', which undercuts the 'good view' claim

baselines.name: Tuned hand-picked augmentation (grid over {jitter, scaling, permutation, crop, masking} and pairwise combinations)
baselines.why: the baseline that matters, because the claim is 'no trial-and-error'

tuning.space: {jitter, scaling, permutation, crop, masking} and pairwise combinations; same tuning budget in GPU-hours as our method's hyperparameter search (Run 3)

baselines.name: Random-mask control (h ~ Bernoulli(π̄), g resampled from the learned-g marginal, no augmentation network)
η-only ablation (h = 1, g = 1, hidden-layer masking only)
baselines.why: separates the noise function from the learned masks

metrics.name: mse (normalized, averaged over the 5 horizons, per dataset)

statistics.repeatUnit: seed, paired across arms (same seed controls data order and probe)
statistics.test: 95% CI of the paired per-seed difference; must exclude 0 on at least 3 of 4 datasets
statistics.notes: forecasting gains between contrastive methods are often 1-5% MSE, about the size of seed variance, so 3 seeds cannot resolve them

hyperparameters.notes: all hyperparameters for every arm (β, λ, α, M, η, the augmentation grid, ridge α) are chosen on val; our method's sweep covers β, M and η masking probability

protocol.postprocessing: frozen encoder + ridge-regression probe (TS2Vec repo evaluation protocol assumed: ridge probe, padding, horizons)

stages.name: Run 1: our method with mask logging
stages.gate: h not ≈ all-1 or all-0; g not ≈ constant; the MMD term does not go to 0 trivially

stages.name: Run 3: validation sweep of our method
Run 4: hand-picked augmentation grid, budget matched to Run 3
Run 5: final runs, test read once

risks.text: Run 1 is the most likely failure point: with β too high h -> 0, and through the MMD term the augmentation network can learn g ≈ constant scaling that the encoder ignores
risks.mitigation: look at the Run 1 logs before spending compute on sweeps
